articles.title: US immigration agency on 'guarantee' that you can get a American visa, Green Card, or work permit faster: Sometimes businesses and websites ...
articles.summary: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has warned immigrants and visa applicants not to fall for businesses, websites, or individuals that
articles.body: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has warned immigrants and visa applicants not to fall for businesses, websites, or individuals that claim they can secure faster approvals for visas, Green Cards, or work permits in exchange for a fee. According to the agency, such promises are often signs of immigration scams. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) USCIS wrote, “ IT'S A SCAM: Sometimes businesses and websites pretend to be immigration experts or say they have special connections to the government. They might also “guarantee” that you can get a visa, Green Card, or work permit faster if you pay a fee.”USCIS warns against false promisesThe agency said applicants should be cautious of anyone claiming to have a special relationship with the US government or USCIS that can influence immigration decisions. USCIS notes that immigration benefits are processed through official procedures and warns that no private individual or organisation can guarantee a specific outcome or accelerated processing simply because of claimed government connections.USCIS also stressed that applicants do not need a representative to file immigration forms and may submit applications on their own. Those seeking assistance should work only with qualified attorneys or accredited representatives recognised by the US Department of Justice.Be aware that scammers:•Try to confuse you by complicating the immigration process;•Use social media, email, or phone calls to conduct their attacks; and•Impersonate government officials to manipulate the victim into giving out personal information.How applicants can protect themselvesAs part of its anti-fraud guidance, USCIS encourages applicants to verify information through official government websites, obtain written agreements for any legal services, keep copies of immigration forms and records, and be wary of offers that sound too good to be true. The agency maintains an online resource to help immigrants identify and avoid common scams and fraud schemes.Be cautious of:•Emails that look legitimate, but are sent by people you don’t know;•Emails with typos and incorrect spellings;•E-mails that do not end in .gov and end in (.net, .org, .com, or .info for example)•Suspicious emails you don’t normally receive;•Offers of assistance to expedite your case for money;•Promises of a quick benefit; and•Downloading or opening attachments from senders you don’t recognize.; and•Requests from USCIS to transfer money to an individual or pay fees other than through your myUSCIS accountYou use AI every day. articles.title: Cowboys Defense Must Prove its Meeting Meant Something
articles.summary: The Cowboys defense held an honest meeting after its latest loss. Now Dallas must turn accountability into better execution against the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
The Cowboys defense has discussed what it wants to become. Against the Green Bay Packers, it must begin showing whether those conversations can change its performance.

Following the Week 5 loss to Tampa Bay, Dallas' defensive players took time to examine their standards and responsibilities. DeMarvion Overshown described the Monday, October 12 meeting as an opportunity to evaluate themselves and discuss how they could hep one another.

That conversation offers a meaningful starting point. However, its value will depend on whether Dallas communicates more clearly, handles assignments more consistently and prevent manageable plays from becoming costly mistakes.

Cowboys Defense Takes an Honest Look at its Standards

According to Overshown, the defense wrote its expectations on a board and reviewed them individually. Players considered whether their performances matched those expectations and what they needed from their teammates during preparation and games.

"What can I do to help you?" was one of the questions Overshown used to explain the discussion. His account emphasized cooperation and accountability rather than panic or accusations.

That distinction matters. A productive meeting should give players specific responsibilities they can carry into practice. General promises about effort provide little direction unless teammates understand what must change and how to recognize improvement.

For Dallas, accountability should also extend beyond the players nearest the ball when a players breaks down. Coaches and defenders must identify how positioning, communication and execution contribution to the result before deciding on a correction.

The Problems Requires More than Better Intentions

Through five games, Dallas ranked 31st in total defense , allowing 395.4 yards per game. That performance helps explain the urgency surrounding a team preparing for Green Bay with a 2-3 record.

The defensive breakdowns against Tampa Bay made another review necessary. The challenge now is to translate the discussion into preparation that produces reliable answers when opponents attack the same weaknesses.

Overshown identified mental errors as an obstacle and expressed confidence in the unit's potential. That confidence represents a player's assessment, rather than evidence that the defense has already turned a corner.

Against Green Bay, useful signs would include defenders getting aligned before the snap, maintaining their responsibilities against motion and finishing tackles after making initial contact. Those details offer a more practical measure of progress than emotional reactions after an isolated stop.

The response to a succesfull opposing drive will matter, too. Dallas must identify what worked against it, communicate a correction and execute that correction before the same problem damages another possession.

Coaching Support Must Produce Clearer Answers

The addition of Mike Pettine to the defensive staff gives Christian Parker another experienced resource. Pettine joined as a senior defensive assistant after previously working with both Parker and Brian Schottenheimer.

His arrival and the players' meeting address different parts of the same challenge. Coaches must provide assignments players can understand and execute, while defenders must communicate uncertainty before it becomes a mistake during a game.

Adding more instructions will not necessarily create better football. The staff should prioritize corrections that players can repeat under pressure, particularly when the offense changes its formation or forces a quick decision.

That responsibility also belongs to Schottenheimer as the leader of the entire team. He must ensure the defensive changes produce a coherent plan and that practice reinforces the standards players discussed

The Cowboys defense must play with urgency, toughness, and pride against Green Bay. After an honest conversation about their standards, players need to show that accountability through their effort: pursuing the ball, finishing tackles, and staying disciplined when the game gets difficult.

Emotion alone will not fix missed assignments, but Dallas needs its intensity and execution to match. Sunday offers this group an opportunity to back up its words with a performance that earns back some trust.

The players have examined what they expect from one another. Can they now make those expectations visible on the field?

articles.title: TV broadcast map for Bears vs. Falcons in Week 6
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears will battle the Atlanta Falcons in Week 6. See if the game will be on in your part of the country.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears will face the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, where Chicago is looking to get back in the win column after a disappointing loss in Week 5.

The Bears are coming off a brutal 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers , where offense, defense, special teams and coaching all struggled. Now, the attention shifts to a key NFC matchup against the Falcons, where Chicago is expected to get back quarterback Caleb Williams, who's missed the last three games due to a hamstring injury.

Let's see if the Bears will be on in your part of the country.

Bears vs. Packers: Photos from Chicago's Week 5 loss

If you live in the red area of the map, you'll be able to watch Bears-Falcons locally at 12 p.m. CT on FOX ( via 506sports.com ).

Most of the country will get the Bears-Falcons (red) game. The rest of the country will get New Orleans Saints - New York Giants (blue), Baltimore Ravens - Cleveland Browns (green) and Tennessee Titans- Indianapolis Colts (orange) as part of FOX's early slate of games.

Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady will be on the Bears-Falcons call for FOX.

The Bears and Falcons kick things off Sunday at 12 p.m. CT on FOX.

articles.title: Popular Florida pro-am that attracts PGA Tour players, other pros turns 50
articles.summary: The Henry Tuten Gator Bowl Pro-Am reaches a milestone this year. And it will be a bittersweet celebration, without the tournament's namesake.
articles.body:
The Henry Tuten Gator Bowl Pro-Am reaches a milestone this year. And it will be a bittersweet celebration, without the tournament's namesake.

The holiday staple on the area's golf schedule will be Dec. 14-15 at the Sea Island Resort Seaside and Plantation Courses on St. Simons Island, Georgia. It will be the 50th playing of the tournament, which annually has attracted pros from the PGA Tour, PGA Tour Champions, LIV, Korn Ferry Tour, PGA Tour Americas and club professionals from Florida's First Coast and Georgia's Golden Isles.

Each pro is grouped with three amateurs and played 36 holes under a gross best ball.

Early commitments to play are PGA Tour winners Russell Knox, Keith Mitchell, Andrew Novak, Harold Varner III and Taylor Dickson.

Participants in the past have included World Golf Hall of Fame member Vijay Singh, Players Championship winners David Duval, Mark McCumber and Cameron Smith, and PGA Tour winners Len Mattiace, Kenny Perry, Frank Lickliter and Davis Thompson.

Tournament organizers will use its 50th anniversary to honor Tuten, who passed away in March at the age of 97. One of his legacies is more than $100,000 in charitable giving over the last six years to area golf-themed non-profits.

articles.title: DP World India Championship: Eugenio Chacarra leads but Rory McIlroy fades before play halted
articles.summary: Eugenio Chacarra extends his lead at the DP World India Championship but Rory McIlroy loses ground before the third round is halted because of darkness.
articles.body:
DP World India Championship, round three leaderboard

14 E Chacarra (Spa) (11*); -12 J Luiten (Ned) (12*), A Hidalgo (Spa) (11*); -11 D Hillier (NZ) (14*), A Meronk (Pol) (11*), S Jamieson (Sco) (11*); -10 T McKibbin (NI) (14*), JC Ritchie (SA) (14*), T Clements (Eng) (12*), J Girrbach (Swi) (12*)

Selected others: -9 T Fleetwood (Eng); -8 R MacIntyre (Sco) (13*), D Bradbury (Eng); -7 S Lowry (Ire), L Canter (Eng); -6 P Reed (US) (13*), E Pepperell (Eng) (12*), M Armitage (Eng); -5 A Rai (Eng) (14*) -4 R McIlroy (NI) (15*); -2 J Rose (Eng) (11*)

*Denotes number of holes played before play ended on day one

Eugenio Chacarra extended his lead at the DP World India Championship but Rory McIlroy lost ground before the third round was halted because of darkness.

Spain's Chacarra led by one shot at 10 under after two rounds at the weather-hit event at Delhi Golf Club and sits two clear after 11 holes of his third round.

After successive rounds of 67, the 26-year-old birdied four of his opening seven holes to cement his place at the top as he bids to replace American Patrick Reed at the summit of the season-long Race to Dubai rankings.

Fellow Spaniard Angel Hidalgo and the Netherlands' Joost Luisten are his closest challengers at 12 under, with Scotland's Scott Jamieson a shot further back.

Northern Ireland's Tom McKibbin is four adrift with defending champion Tommy Fleetwood five back after a four-under 68.

Scotland's Robert MacIntyre is also well placed at eight under with five holes of his third round remaining.

However, McIlroy - who sits third in the Race to Dubai behind Reed and Chacarra - fell 10 shots off the lead after an erratic third round.

Having completed a bogey-free second-round 68 early on Saturday, the six-time major winner birdied his opening hole before dropping four shots in as many holes from the third.

After a birdie on the seventh, McIlroy made back-to-back bogeys on the ninth and 10th before sensationally holing out from the bunker for an eagle three at the 14th.

Reed played the first 13 holes of his third round to sit two shots ahead of McIlroy.

The 2018 Masters champion, who tops the Race to Dubai rankings after early-season victories in Dubai and Qatar, mixed five birdies and a bogey before holing his 150-yard approach shot for a spectacular eagle two at the fourth, having teed off at the 10th.

articles.title: Eugenio Chacarra, más líder en la India
articles.standfirst: Afianza su primer puesto, con dos golpes de ventaja sobre Joost Luiten y Ángel Hidalgo, durante una tercera ronda que quedó sin concluir
articles.summary: Afianza su primer puesto, con dos golpes de ventaja sobre Joost Luiten y Ángel Hidalgo, durante una tercera ronda que quedó sin concluir
articles.body: Eugenio López-Chacarra se mantiene como líder del DP World India, en Nueva Delhi, tras una tercera jornada inconclusa por la falta de luz. El español se citó con el campo al alba (6.40 de la mañana) para, primero, acabar los hoyos pendientes de la segunda ronda. Tras otra tarjeta de 67 golpes se instaló en la cabeza en solitario con 10 bajo par, con uno de ventaja sobre el escocés Scott Jamieson. Poco después, arrancó el tercer recorrido. López-Chacarra completó 11 hoyos en los que firmó cuatro birdies (nueve en total en el día tras los cinco logrados en el desenlace de la segunda ronda) para colocarse 14 bajo par. Este resultado afianza su liderato. Amplía su ventaja sobre sus perseguidores: dos golpes sobre el holandés Joost Luiten (completó un hoyo más) y Ángel Hidalgo, que jugó en el mismo partido que Chacarra (Resultados). El DP World India ha ido a remolque desde el retraso de casi cinco horas en el inicio de la primera jornada. Este domingo Chacarra y el resto de jugadores volverán al campo para completar la tercera ronda desde las 06:35 de la mañana antes de afrontar los últimos 18 hoyos del torneo. Chacarra está más cerca de encabezar la clasificación Race to Dubai por delante del actual líder de la temporada, Patrick Reed, que pasó el corte con apuros, pero terminó el día seis bajo par, y de Rory McIlroy, que va cuatro abajo tras completar 15 hoyos en la tercera ronda con un +2. Eso sí, dejó un eagle desde el bunker en el 14. Si Chacarra gana este domingo lideraría la Race a falta de tres torneos (Corea, Abu Dhabi y Dubái) y estaría por primera vez entre los 40 mejores del ránking mundial lo que le aseguraría un billete para el Masters de Augusta. Al español se le da bien jugar en India. En 2025 ganó el Hero Indian Open y este año, en marzo, fue segundo.

articles.title: DP World India Championship: Rory McIlroy drops 10 shots off the lead as Eugenio Chacarra moving into position for another big win
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy drops out of contention - 10 shots off leader Eugenio Chacarra - with Saturday's play suspended because of fading light, with most of the field yet to finish their third round
articles.body:
Chacarra was leading by two strokes on 14 under when Saturday's play was suspended because of fading light, with most of the field yet to finish their third round.

The Spaniard was four under for his round after 11 holes, having started out in the halfway lead after completing a second-round 67 early Saturday.

Joost Luiten was four under after 12 holes and Angel Hidalgo four under after 11 holes, with both players tied for second place on 12 under par.

Daniel Hillier, Adrian Meronk and Scott Jamieson were a further shot back.

Patrick Reed and McIlroy - battling with Chacarra for the season-long Race to Dubai title - were eight and 10 shots off the lead, respectively.

Chacarra earned one of the biggest wins of his career in India last year, triumphing at the Hero Indian Open - where he was playing on an invitation - to earn his full status on the European tour.

He had previously been on the LIV Golf circuit.

Play will restart at 6.35am local time on Sunday, with Chacarra needing to play the remaining seven holes of his third round as well as his entire final round.
